title: Adjective + preposition 2
subtitle: afraid of / good at / interested in
summary: Learn which preposition follows adjectives like afraid, proud, good, married, similar, interested, keen and famous.

lesson.heading: afraid of, proud of, jealous of
lesson.text: We say **afraid / scared / frightened / terrified of ...** and **fond / proud / ashamed / jealous / envious of ...**.

examples.text: 'Are you **afraid of** spiders?' 'Yes, I'm **terrified of** them.'
Why is he so **jealous of** other people?
Kate is very **fond of** her younger brother.

lesson.heading: aware of, capable of, full of
lesson.text: We also use **of** after **suspicious / critical / tolerant**, **aware / conscious**, **capable / incapable**, **full / short** and **typical**. **Certain** and **sure** take **of** or **about**.

examples.text: They didn't trust me. They were **suspicious of** my motives.
'Did you know he was married?' 'No, I wasn't **aware of** that.'
I'm sure you are **capable of** doing the job well.
Amy is a very active person. She's always **full of** energy.
I'm a bit **short of** money. Can you lend me some?
He's late again. It's **typical of** him to keep everybody waiting.
I think she's arriving this evening, but I'm not **sure of** that.

lesson.heading: good at, married to, similar to
lesson.text: We say **good / bad / brilliant / better / hopeless at ...**, **married / engaged to ...** and **similar to ...**. **Different** takes **from** or **to**.

examples.text: I'm not very **good at** repairing things.
The film was **different from** what I'd expected.
examples.note: or ... different to what I'd expected

lesson.note: But: Louise is married **with** three children. (= she is married and has three children)

lesson.heading: interested in, keen on, dependent on
lesson.text: We say **interested in ...**, **keen on ...** and **dependent on ...** (but **independent of ...**).

examples.text: We stayed at home. Chris wasn't **keen on** going out.
I don't want to be **dependent on** anybody.
Mark has no money of his own. He's completely **dependent on** his parents.

lesson.heading: crowded with or full of?
lesson.note: We also say **famous for ...** and **responsible for ...**: The Italian city of Florence is **famous for** its art treasures. Who was **responsible for** all that noise last night?

lesson.text: Watch the pairs that learners mix up: good **at** (not in), married **to** (not with), and crowded **with** but full **of**.

exercises.prompt: I'm a bit ___ money. Can you lend me some?
exercises.explanation: Short of something = not having enough of it.

exercises.prompt: My children have done very well. I'm ___ them.
exercises.explanation: Proud of, like fond of, ashamed of and jealous of.

exercises.prompt: I'm not very good ___ repairing things.
exercises.explanation: Good, bad, brilliant and hopeless all take at.

exercises.prompt: Steven's wife is a doctor. Steven is married ___.
exercises.explanation: Married to somebody (but married with three children = has three children).

exercises.prompt: Match the two halves of the sentences.

pairs.left: We stayed at home. Chris wasn't keen
The city of Florence is famous
The editor is the person who is responsible
pairs.right: for what appears in a newspaper

exercises.prompt: I was surprised when I first met Tina. She was different ___ what I expected.
exercises.explanation: Different from (or different to) - never different of.

exercises.prompt: There was a lot of furniture in the room. The room was full ___.
exercises.explanation: Full of something, but crowded with something.

exercises.statement: The streets were crowded of tourists.
exercises.explanation: The streets were crowded with tourists. Only full takes of.

exercises.prompt: Mark has no money of his own. He's completely dependent ___ his parents.
exercises.explanation: Dependent on somebody (but independent of somebody).

exercises.prompt: These days everybody is aware ___ the dangers of smoking.
exercises.explanation: Aware of and conscious of something.

exercises.prompt: I don't trust Robert. I'm suspicious ___.
exercises.explanation: Suspicious of, like critical of and tolerant of.
